about: The moth's hull lines (docs/moth-2): a few curves along her length that hull_moth.py turns into sections. Frame: x forward from the hull's middle (stem +1.6775, transom -1.6775: the class's 3,355 mm), y to one side from the centreline, z up from the keel's lowest point; hull_moth.py moves z to the design waterline once it has solved where she floats. Shape read by eye from the CC BY / PD photos in refs.json (the flying broadside, the boat on her side, the two on trolleys): nothing traced. An invented hull inside the class rules, not any builder's.

keel.note: The keel line, as height above its lowest point: almost straight (a moth's hull only matters at rest and at take-off), a plumb stem carried nearly to the keel with only a small forefoot radius (the afloat photo shows a tall, nearly upright bow; Milestone A cut the forefoot from 0.2 m to 0.11 m and the transom's rise from 0.06 to 0.035, after all three reviewers read the bow as rounded), a little rise to the transom. Points are (x, z). Milestone B raised the transom's rise again, 0.035 to 0.07 (with the lower aft sheer: every reviewer read the aft hull as too deep).

sheer.note: The deck edge's height above the keel's lowest point (x, z): highest near the bow (she noses into waves when low-riding), lower toward the transom so the sailor can sit back. Milestone B lowered it all along, most aft (bow 0.452 to 0.405, x -0.2 0.435 to 0.355, transom 0.40 to 0.27): six of six reviewers over two rounds read the hull as 25-60% too deep, most of it aft, and the hull's outline laid over the camera-matched flying photo showed the real hull about 0.37 m deep at the bow and 0.2 m at the transom. Round 3 read the sheer as flat where the photos' deck sweeps up to the bow; lowering the deck at the mast to show it moved the mast's foot 10 px off the camera-matched photo (from 6), so the sheer stays and the raised look comes from the fairing at the mast's foot (hardware_moth.json).

plan.note: Half-breadth at the deck edge (x, y): widest a little aft of the middle, a fine bow, a broad transom for the gantry's feet. Milestone B widened the aft quarter a little (transom 0.135 to 0.15 a side) to float the shallower stern.

section.note: Each section is a V that rounds into upright topsides: half-breadth at height t (0 keel, 1 deck edge) is plan(x) * t^power, the power smaller (fuller, rounder) aft and larger (sharper V) forward. deadrise_flat rounds the keel over its lowest few cm; deck_crown is how high the deck's middle stands over its edges; edge_round the deck edge's radius. Milestone B made the sections fuller and the bilge harder (powers 0.32/0.40/0.62 to 0.16/0.22/0.45, keel round 12 to 8 mm, deck edge round 18 to 10 mm): reviewers read the bottom corners as soft, the real hulls as slab-sided with crisp chines, and fuller sections float her shallower so the lower deck keeps its freeboard (three reviewers in round 3 still saw her float about half as high as the afloat photo).
